stem: A single taxpayer's 2024 AGI was $140,000 and 2024 tax was $22,000. Her 2025 tax will be $35,000 and withholding will be $15,000. What minimum estimated payments avoid the underpayment penalty?

choices.explanation: Uses 100% of current-year tax.
Uses 90% of current-year tax.
Uses 110% of prior-year tax, but AGI didn't exceed $150,000.
Correct. Required payment = lesser of 31,500 or 22,000; 22,000 − 15,000.

explanation: 100% of prior-year tax applies because prior AGI was ≤ $150,000.

stem: Which item is included in net investment income for the 3.8% NIIT?

choices.text: Wages paid to her by an S corporation
choices.explanation: Wages aren't NII.
Social Security isn't investment income.

choices.text: Qualified distributions from a Roth IRA
choices.explanation: Retirement distributions are excluded.

choices.text: Gain on the sale of a vacation home
choices.explanation: Correct. Gain on disposition of property not held in an active business is NII.

explanation: Gain on disposition of property not held in an active business is NII.

stem: A married couple filing jointly has MAGI of $270,000, including $40,000 of net investment income. What is their NIIT?

choices.explanation: Uses NII instead of the smaller MAGI excess.
MAGI exceeds $250,000.
Uses the $200,000 threshold.

explanation: Base = lesser of 40,000 NII or 20,000 excess → 3.8% × 20,000 = 760.

stem: For 2025 the kiddie-tax threshold is $2,700. A 17-year-old full-time high school student has $10,000 of dividend income in 2025 and no earned income. How much is taxed at the parents' rate?

choices.explanation: The kiddie tax applies.
The first $2,700 isn't taxed at the parents' rate.
Subtracts only $1,350.

explanation: 2025 kiddie tax threshold: $2,700.

stem: Which planning step most likely reduces a client's AGI while satisfying her charitable goal and her 2025 RMD (age 74)?

choices.text: Donate appreciated stock she has held for 5 years
choices.explanation: Deduction, but not an AGI exclusion or an RMD.

choices.text: Donate cash from a taxable brokerage account
choices.explanation: Itemized deduction only.

choices.text: Make a qualified charitable distribution from the IRA
choices.explanation: Correct. QCDs are excluded from income and count toward the RMD.

choices.text: Take the RMD and give it to a donor-advised fund
choices.explanation: The RMD still increases AGI.

explanation: QCDs are excluded from income and count toward the RMD.

stem: An employee exercises NQSOs on 200 shares at $25 when FMV is $70 and sells 14 months later at $60. What are the results?

choices.explanation: Income is measured at exercise.
That's ISO-style treatment.
Held more than 1 year after exercise.
Correct. Ordinary = (70 − 25) × 200 = 9,000; basis 14,000; sale 12,000 → 2,000 long-term loss.

explanation: Ordinary = (70 − 25) × 200 = 9,000; basis 14,000; sale 12,000 → 2,000 long-term loss.

stem: ISO shares are exercised at a $12 strike when FMV is $32 and held into the next year. What is the effect in the year of exercise?

choices.text: $20 per share of wages in that year
choices.explanation: ISO exercise produces no wages.
No sale occurred.
Correct. §56(b)(3): the ISO spread at exercise is a positive AMT adjustment; regular tax is deferred until sale.

choices.text: No effect for regular tax or AMT
choices.explanation: AMT is affected.

explanation: §56(b)(3): the ISO spread at exercise is a positive AMT adjustment; regular tax is deferred until sale.

stem: A founder receives 100,000 restricted shares worth $0.10 each, vesting in 4 years. Which statement about a §83(b) election is correct?

choices.text: It converts the restricted shares into ISOs
choices.explanation: Restricted stock doesn't become an option.

choices.text: It defers all income until the shares are sold
choices.explanation: The election accelerates income.

choices.text: It can be filed when the shares finally vest
choices.explanation: The deadline is 30 days after transfer.

choices.text: Filed within 30 days; $10,000 of income now
choices.explanation: Correct. §83(b): elect within 30 days; income = FMV − amount paid at transfer.

explanation: §83(b): elect within 30 days; income = FMV − amount paid at transfer.

stem: A single taxpayer with MAGI of $110,000 actively participates in a rental that lost $28,000. She has no passive income. How much loss is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance is reduced.
Limited by the allowance.
The allowance applies.

stem: A taxpayer has $50,000 of passive income from a limited partnership and a $70,000 loss from another passive business activity. What is the result?

choices.explanation: Limited to passive income.
Passive losses offset passive income.
The $25,000 allowance is for rental real estate.
Correct. Passive losses offset passive income; the excess carries forward.

explanation: Passive losses offset passive income; the excess carries forward.

stem: Which taxpayer's rental losses are **not** automatically passive?

choices.text: A doctor who owns and actively manages two rentals
choices.explanation: Rentals are passive unless an exception applies.

choices.text: A retiree with a rental managed by a property agent
choices.explanation: Rentals managed by an agent are passive.

choices.text: A real estate pro who materially participates
choices.explanation: Correct. §469(c)(7): a real estate professional's rentals with material participation are not passive.

choices.text: An investor in a real estate limited partnership
choices.explanation: Limited partners are generally passive.

explanation: §469(c)(7): a real estate professional's rentals with material participation are not passive.

stem: A beach condo is rented 200 days and used personally 25 days. How is it treated?

choices.text: Rental property, with no personal-use limits
choices.explanation: 25 days exceeds the greater of 14 days or 20 days.
Not the classification issue.

choices.text: The rent is excluded from gross income
choices.explanation: Rented more than 14 days.

choices.text: Residence; deductions limited to rental income
choices.explanation: Correct. Personal use of 25 days > greater of 14 or 10% × 200 = 20 → residence.

explanation: Personal use of 25 days > greater of 14 or 10% × 200 = 20 → residence.

stem: The 2025 gift tax annual exclusion is $19,000 per donee. In 2025, an unmarried donor gives $25,000 to each of her three grandchildren and pays $40,000 directly to a hospital for one of them. What are her taxable gifts?

choices.explanation: Exclusions apply.
Direct medical payments are excluded.
Each gift exceeds the exclusion.

explanation: Annual exclusion $19,000 per donee; medical payments made directly are excluded.

stem: Which gift is a present interest eligible for the annual exclusion?

choices.text: A remainder interest in a trust
choices.explanation: Remainders are future interests.
A reversion is a future interest.

choices.text: A gift to a trust that accumulates income until the beneficiary turns 30, without withdrawal rights
choices.explanation: No immediate right to enjoy it.

choices.text: Cash transferred to a UTMA account for a minor
choices.explanation: Correct. UTMA gifts are treated as present interests.

explanation: UTMA gifts are treated as present interests.

stem: A donor gives land (basis $70,000; FMV $100,000) and pays $12,000 of gift tax. The taxable gift was $81,000. What is the donee's basis?

choices.explanation: Gift tax on the appreciation is added.
Adds all the gift tax.
FMV isn't the basis.

explanation: §1015(d)(6): add gift tax attributable to net appreciation.

stem: A couple elects gift splitting for 2025. Which statement is true?

choices.text: Only the donor spouse needs to file Form 709
choices.explanation: Both generally file when splitting.

choices.text: Splitting doubles the lifetime exemption only
choices.explanation: It applies to the annual exclusion and exemption.

choices.text: Splitting can be elected gift by gift
choices.explanation: It applies to all gifts for the year.

choices.text: It covers all gifts to third parties that year
choices.explanation: Correct. §2513 consent applies to all gifts to third parties during the calendar year.

explanation: §2513 consent applies to all gifts to third parties during the calendar year.

stem: For 2025 the 401(k) elective deferral limit is $23,500, the age-50 catch-up is $7,500, and the enhanced catch-up for ages 60–63 is $11,250. What is the maximum elective deferral for a 62-year-old employee?

choices.explanation: Catch-ups apply.
The higher catch-up applies at ages 60–63.
That's the total additions limit.

explanation: SECURE 2.0 enhanced catch-up for ages 60–63: $11,250 (2025).

stem: A self-employed individual's Schedule C profit is $120,000 and her deduction for half of SE tax is $8,478. What is her maximum SEP contribution?

choices.explanation: Uses 25% of Schedule C profit.
That's the 401(k) deferral limit.
Limited by the percentage.

explanation: 20% of net earnings after the SE tax deduction.

stem: A 35-year-old withdraws $8,000 from a traditional IRA to pay qualified college tuition for herself. What is the tax effect?

choices.explanation: Correct. §72(t)(2)(E): higher education exception for IRAs.
Traditional IRA distributions are taxable.
The education exception applies to IRAs.
Withdrawals are allowed.

explanation: §72(t)(2)(E): higher education exception for IRAs.

stem: Which statement about Roth IRAs is correct?

choices.text: Owners must begin RMDs at age 73
choices.explanation: Roth IRAs have no lifetime RMDs.

choices.text: There is no income limit on contributions
choices.explanation: Contributions phase out.
Roth contributions are after-tax.
Correct. Ordering rules: regular contributions come out first, tax- and penalty-free.

explanation: Ordering rules: regular contributions come out first, tax- and penalty-free.

stem: Parents with MAGI of $100,000 (MFJ) pay $3,000 of qualified tuition for their child's first year of college. What is their American opportunity tax credit?

choices.explanation: The full credit requires $4,000 of expenses.
The credit isn't dollar-for-dollar.
Applies the lifetime learning credit rate.

explanation: 100% of the first $2,000 + 25% of the next $2,000.

stem: A single taxpayer with 2025 MAGI of $550,000 pays $50,000 of state and local taxes. What is her SALT deduction?

choices.explanation: The cap is reduced above $500,000 MAGI.
The deduction is capped.
The floor applies only if the reduction goes further.

explanation: P.L. 119-21: $40,000 cap reduced by 30% of MAGI over $500,000, not below $10,000.
reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount or effective date. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

stem: A partner has outside basis of $30,000, is at risk for $20,000, and her passive share of loss is $(35,000). She has no passive income. How much can she deduct?

choices.explanation: At-risk and passive limits also apply.
The passive limit still applies.
Correct. After basis (30,000) and at-risk (20,000), the passive limit suspends the rest because there is no passive income.
Several limits apply.

explanation: After basis (30,000) and at-risk (20,000), the passive limit suspends the rest because there is no passive income.

stem: A widow wants to transfer an asset expected to appreciate greatly to her son. From an income tax perspective, when is a gift during life least favorable compared with a bequest at death?

choices.text: Low-basis asset the son may sell soon after her death
choices.explanation: Correct. Gifted property keeps the donor's low basis; inherited property gets a stepped-up basis (§1014).

choices.text: When the asset's basis exceeds its fair market value
choices.explanation: A bequest would step the basis down, too.

choices.text: When the asset is cash in a bank account
choices.explanation: Cash has no built-in gain.

choices.text: It never matters for income tax purposes
choices.explanation: Basis rules differ.

explanation: Gifted property keeps the donor's low basis; inherited property gets a stepped-up basis (§1014).

stem: Which corporation is subject to the corporate alternative minimum tax?

choices.text: Average adjusted financial statement income over $1 billion
choices.explanation: Correct. CAMT applies to applicable corporations with average AFSI over $1 billion.

choices.text: Any corporation with taxable income over $1 million
choices.explanation: The test is AFSI over $1 billion.

choices.text: An S corporation with large book income
choices.explanation: S corporations aren't subject.

choices.text: A small corporation with large NOL carryforwards
choices.explanation: Size, not NOLs, drives CAMT.

explanation: CAMT applies to applicable corporations with average AFSI over $1 billion.

stem: A parent owns 80% of the voting power but only 70% of the value of a subsidiary. Can they file a consolidated return?

choices.explanation: Both tests must be met.
Correct. §1504(a)(2): at least 80% of vote AND value.
Consent can't cure failed ownership.

choices.text: Only if the subsidiary is foreign
choices.explanation: Foreign subsidiaries are excluded.

explanation: §1504(a)(2): at least 80% of vote AND value.

stem: A group member sells equipment to another member at a $30,000 gain; the buyer depreciates it over 5 years. How is the seller's gain taken into account?

choices.text: All in the year of the intercompany sale
choices.explanation: Intercompany gain is deferred.

choices.text: As the buyer depreciates the stepped-up basis
choices.explanation: Correct. Matching rule: the seller's gain offsets the buyer's extra depreciation over time.
It's taken into account under the matching rule.

choices.text: Only when the consolidated group liquidates
choices.explanation: It's taken in as depreciation occurs.

explanation: Matching rule: the seller's gain offsets the buyer's extra depreciation over time.

stem: A contributes land (basis $40,000; FMV $100,000) subject to a $30,000 liability to a new 50/50 partnership. B contributes $70,000 cash. The liability is shared equally. What is A's outside basis?

choices.explanation: Ignores liabilities.
Omits A's share of the liability.
That's net FMV.

explanation: Basis = 40,000 − 30,000 relief + 15,000 share.

stem: A partner receives a 20% capital interest (FMV $50,000) solely for services. What is the result?

choices.text: No income; a $0 basis in the interest
choices.explanation: A capital interest for services is taxable.
Correct. Compensation income equals the FMV of the capital interest.
It's compensation.

choices.text: Income deferred until the interest is sold
choices.explanation: It's taxed when received.

explanation: Compensation income equals the FMV of the capital interest.

stem: A partnership's only partners are corporations X (45%, June 30 year-end), Y (30%, June 30), and Z (25%, December 31). What is the required tax year?

choices.explanation: The majority interest uses June 30.
Correct. X and Y hold 75%.
Majority interest applies first.
It must use the required year absent an exception.

explanation: §706(b)(1)(B)(i): majority-interest tax year.

stem: A partner's share of partnership items: ordinary income $20,000; §179 expense $5,000; charitable contributions $2,000. Beginning basis $10,000; no distributions. What is ending basis?

choices.explanation: Omits the deductions.
Omits the charitable contribution and part of §179.
Omits beginning basis.

stem: A partnership pays a partner a $40,000 guaranteed payment for services. The partnership's calendar year ends December 31, 2025; the partner's year also ends December 31. When and how does the partner report it?

choices.text: 2025, as ordinary income subject to SE tax
choices.explanation: Correct. §707(c) and §706(a).

choices.text: 2025, as wages reported on a Form W-2
choices.explanation: Partners don't get W-2s.

choices.text: When paid, as long-term capital gain
choices.explanation: Guaranteed payments are ordinary income.

choices.text: Never; it reduces the partner's basis
choices.explanation: It's income and doesn't change basis.

stem: A partner (outside basis $45,000) receives a current distribution of $10,000 cash and property with a partnership basis of $50,000. What is the property's basis to the partner?

choices.explanation: Limited to remaining outside basis.
Cash reduces basis first.
Remaining basis is assigned.

stem: In a liquidating distribution, a partner with $60,000 of outside basis receives $15,000 cash and inventory with a partnership basis of $20,000. What is the result?

choices.explanation: Inventory can't be stepped up.
A loss is allowed with only cash and inventory.
The loss is capital.

stem: A partner sells her interest for $90,000; outside basis is $50,000. Her share of the partnership's depreciation recapture potential on equipment is $15,000. What is her ordinary income?

choices.explanation: Recapture is a §751 hot asset.
Correct. Depreciation recapture is an unrealized receivable under §751(c).
Only the §751 share is ordinary.
That's the capital portion.

explanation: Depreciation recapture is an unrealized receivable under §751(c).

stem: A corporation has 95 shareholders, including a husband and wife, and an estate. One shareholder is a nonresident alien. Is it eligible for S status?

choices.explanation: Nonresident aliens are ineligible shareholders.

choices.text: No — a nonresident alien is a shareholder

choices.explanation: Estates are eligible.

choices.text: No, because the spouses count as two shareholders
choices.explanation: Spouses count as one, and either way it's under 100.

stem: An S corporation shareholder has stock basis of $0 and debt basis of $0 from a $20,000 loan after prior losses. This year her share of income is $12,000. Which basis is restored first?

choices.explanation: Debt basis is restored first.
Correct. §1367(b)(2)(B): net increases restore debt basis first.
Debt basis comes first.

choices.text: Neither — income flows through without adjusting basis
choices.explanation: Income restores basis.

explanation: §1367(b)(2)(B): net increases restore debt basis first.

stem: An S corporation (formerly C) with net unrealized built-in gain of $200,000 at conversion sells an asset in year 3 for a $90,000 recognized built-in gain. Taxable income limitation doesn't apply. What is the built-in gains tax?

choices.explanation: Uses total NUBIG.
The recognition period is 5 years.
Uses a 35% rate instead of 21%.

explanation: §1374: 21% of net recognized built-in gain.

stem: An S corporation has two shareholders: A 60%, B 40%. It distributes $60,000 to A and $10,000 to B. What is the risk?

choices.text: A second class of stock, if rights differ by document
choices.explanation: Correct. Non-pro-rata distributions can raise a second-class-of-stock issue if they reflect different rights under governing provisions.

choices.text: The distributions are automatically taxed as dividends
choices.explanation: Dividend status depends on E&P.

choices.text: B recognizes $30,000 of income on the shortfall
choices.explanation: Income follows ownership, not distributions.

choices.text: None; S corporation distributions are flexible
choices.explanation: Disproportionate distributions raise issues.

explanation: Non-pro-rata distributions can raise a second-class-of-stock issue if they reflect different rights under governing provisions.

stem: A simple trust has DNI of $30,000 (all taxable interest) and distributes all income. What is the trust's taxable income?

choices.explanation: Omits the distribution deduction.
Correct. 30,000 − 30,000 distribution deduction − 300 exemption → 0.
The distribution is deductible.
The exemption reduces income; it doesn't create income.

explanation: 30,000 − 30,000 distribution deduction − 300 exemption → 0.

stem: A decedent died on March 10, 2025. The executor wants to maximize deferral of income for the beneficiaries. Which tax year might the estate choose?

choices.explanation: Estates can choose a fiscal year.
Correct. Estates may adopt a fiscal year ending on the last day of any month within 12 months after death.
A tax year can't exceed 12 months.
The estate is a new taxpayer.

explanation: Estates may adopt a fiscal year ending on the last day of any month within 12 months after death.

stem: Which item is excluded from DNI for a typical trust?

choices.explanation: Interest is part of DNI.

choices.text: Tax-exempt interest, net of related expenses
choices.explanation: Net tax-exempt interest is added to DNI.

choices.text: Capital gains allocated to corpus, not paid out
choices.explanation: Correct. §643(a)(3): capital gains allocated to corpus and not distributed are excluded from DNI and taxed to the trust.
Dividends are part of DNI.

explanation: §643(a)(3): capital gains allocated to corpus and not distributed are excluded from DNI and taxed to the trust.

stem: A §501(c)(3) college operates a bookstore selling textbooks and supplies mainly to students. How is the income treated?

choices.explanation: The convenience exception applies.
Correct. §513(a)(2): activities carried on primarily for the convenience of members, students, or employees.
Bookstore sales to students are excluded.
It's business income, but excluded.

explanation: §513(a)(2): activities carried on primarily for the convenience of members, students, or employees.

stem: A charity normally has gross receipts of $40,000. Which annual return may it file?

choices.explanation: Correct. Gross receipts normally ≤ $50,000 → e-postcard (990-N).
That's for UBTI.
That's for private foundations.
Most organizations must file something.

explanation: Gross receipts normally ≤ $50,000 → e-postcard (990-N).

stem: A single taxpayer with MAGI of $130,000 actively participates in a rental with a $20,000 loss and has no passive income. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance is reduced.
Miscomputes the phase-out.
The allowance isn't fully phased out.

stem: Which item is a tax preference or adjustment for individual AMT?

choices.explanation: Correct. Private activity bond interest is an AMT preference.
Charity is allowed for AMT.
Acquisition interest is allowed for AMT.
Allowed at the same floor for AMT.

explanation: Private activity bond interest is an AMT preference.

stem: A partner with a $15,000 basis receives a current distribution of $5,000 cash and inventory with a partnership basis of $12,000. What is her basis in the inventory?

choices.explanation: Limited by remaining outside basis.
Correct. $15,000 − $5,000 cash.
Outside basis remains after the cash distribution.
Adds instead of limiting.

explanation: Cash first reduces basis to 10,000; inventory takes the lesser of 12,000 or 10,000.

stem: The 2025 gift tax annual exclusion is $19,000 per donee. A donor gives $30,000 to a friend in 2025 and pays $12,000 directly to a hospital for the friend's surgery. What is the taxable gift?

choices.explanation: Medical payments made directly are excluded.
Exclusions apply.
The cash gift exceeds the exclusion.

explanation: Direct medical payments are excluded; the cash gift exceeds the $19,000 exclusion by $11,000.

stem: Which income of a 501(c)(3) organization is most likely UBTI?

choices.explanation: Passive income is excluded.

choices.text: Income from a commercial parking garage it regularly runs
choices.explanation: Correct. A regularly carried-on, unrelated trade or business produces UBTI.

choices.text: Sales of donated goods in its thrift shop
choices.explanation: Donated goods sales are excluded.

choices.text: Proceeds of an annual volunteer-run bake sale
choices.explanation: The volunteer exception applies.

explanation: A regularly carried-on, unrelated trade or business produces UBTI.

stem: A self-employed client will realize a large capital gain in December 2025 and made no estimated payments earlier because her income was low. Which approach can reduce or eliminate an underpayment penalty for the earlier installments?

choices.explanation: Correct. It matches each required installment to income actually earned through that period.

choices.text: Paying the full year's tax on January 15, 2026
choices.explanation: A late payment doesn't cure earlier underpaid installments.

choices.text: Filing a six-month extension for the return
choices.explanation: An extension doesn't extend payment deadlines.

choices.text: Electing to treat the gain as received in 2026
choices.explanation: Timing can't be elected after the sale.

explanation: IRC §6654(d)(2): the annualized income installment method lets a taxpayer with uneven income base installments on income earned through each period.

stem: Which item is excluded from net investment income for the 3.8% NIIT?

choices.text: Rental income from a passive rental activity
choices.explanation: Passive rental income is NII.
Correct. Qualified plan and IRA distributions aren't net investment income.
Dividends are NII.

choices.text: Gain on the sale of investment land
choices.explanation: Gains on investment property are NII.

explanation: IRC §1411(c)(5): distributions from qualified plans and IRAs are excluded from net investment income; wages and active business income are also excluded.

stem: A client expects to move from the 24% bracket in 2025 to the 35% bracket in 2026. Which year-end strategy is most likely to reduce her total tax?

choices.text: Defer income to 2026 and accelerate deductions into 2025
choices.explanation: That reverses the benefit when rates rise.

choices.text: Accelerate both income and deductions into 2025
choices.explanation: Deductions are worth more in the higher-rate year.

choices.text: Accelerate income into 2025 and defer deductions to 2026
choices.explanation: Correct. Income is taxed at the lower 2025 rate, and deductions are worth more at 35%.

choices.text: Defer both income and deductions to 2026
choices.explanation: Income would be taxed at the higher rate.

explanation: When the marginal rate will rise, accelerate income and defer deductions; reverse when rates will fall.

stem: An employee exercises nonqualified stock options for 1,000 shares at $10 when the stock is worth $25. What does she recognize at exercise?

choices.explanation: The spread is ordinary income, not capital gain.

choices.text: Nothing until she sells the shares
choices.explanation: NQSOs are taxed at exercise.
That is the ISO treatment.
Correct. The spread at exercise is compensation; her basis becomes $25 a share.

explanation: IRC §83 and Reg. §1.83-7: nonqualified option spread at exercise is ordinary compensation income, and the employer gets a matching deduction.

stem: An employee exercised ISOs for 100 shares at $20 when the stock was worth $50 and sold them two years later for $70, more than two years after grant. What does she recognize on the sale?

choices.explanation: Correct. A qualifying disposition makes the whole gain (70 − 20) × 100 long-term capital gain.
That is a disqualifying disposition.
Regular-tax basis is the $20 exercise price.
Basis is the exercise price paid.

explanation: IRC §421-422: if ISO stock is held more than 2 years from grant and 1 year from exercise, all gain on sale is long-term capital gain; the spread at exercise is an AMT adjustment only.

stem: An employee receives restricted stock worth $10,000 that vests in three years and makes a timely §83(b) election. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: She recognizes nothing until the stock vests
choices.explanation: That is the result without an election.

choices.text: She recognizes $10,000 of ordinary income now
choices.explanation: Correct. The election accelerates income to the grant date, and later appreciation is capital gain.

choices.text: The election may be made any time before vesting
choices.explanation: It must be made within 30 days of the transfer.

choices.text: All later appreciation will be ordinary income
choices.explanation: After the election, appreciation is capital gain.

explanation: IRC §83(b): an election within 30 days includes the stock's value (less any amount paid) in income at transfer; later appreciation is capital gain when sold.

stem: A taxpayer who actively participates in a rental property has a $22,000 rental loss and 2025 MAGI of $120,000, with no other passive income. How much of the loss is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance is reduced above $100,000 of MAGI.
The deduction can't exceed the loss or the reduced allowance.
Correct. The $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% × (120,000 − 100,000) = 10,000.
Active participants get the special allowance.

explanation: IRC §469(i): up to $25,000 of rental losses for active participants, phased out by 50% of MAGI over $100,000.

stem: An investor contributes $20,000 cash to an equipment-leasing activity, borrows $30,000 for which he is personally liable, and is allocated $50,000 of nonrecourse debt (not qualified real estate financing). What is his amount at risk?

choices.explanation: Nonrecourse debt isn't at risk outside qualified real estate financing.
Recourse borrowing is at risk.
The nonrecourse debt doesn't count.
Correct. Cash plus recourse borrowing; nonrecourse debt isn't at risk.

explanation: IRC §465: amounts at risk include cash and property contributed and borrowings for which the taxpayer is personally liable; nonrecourse debt (other than qualified nonrecourse real estate financing) isn't.

stem: In 2025 a married couple elects gift splitting and gives their daughter $60,000 of cash. The annual exclusion is $19,000 per donee. What are the total taxable gifts?

choices.explanation: Correct. Each spouse is treated as giving 30,000; 30,000 − 19,000 = 11,000 each.
With splitting, each spouse gets an exclusion.
The exclusions reduce taxable gifts.
The gift exceeds two exclusions of $19,000.

explanation: IRC §2513: with gift splitting, each spouse is treated as making half the gift and claims an annual exclusion.

stem: A 45-year-old converts $50,000 from a traditional IRA, funded entirely with deductible contributions, to a Roth IRA in 2025. What are the tax consequences?

choices.text: No income, because the money stays in an IRA
choices.explanation: Conversions of pretax amounts are taxable.
Correct. Conversions are taxable but exempt from the 10% additional tax.
The 10% tax doesn't apply to conversions.
IRA distributions are ordinary income.

explanation: A Roth conversion is a taxable distribution of pretax amounts, but the §72(t) 10% tax doesn't apply to the conversion itself.

stem: The accumulated earnings tax is imposed at what rate, and what minimum credit does a non-service C corporation get?

choices.explanation: The rate is 20%, and $150,000 is for service corporations.
Correct. The AET is 20%, with a $250,000 minimum credit ($150,000 for certain service corporations).
The rate is 20%.
The credit is $250,000.

explanation: IRC §531, §535(c): 20% of accumulated taxable income beyond the reasonable needs of the business, with a $250,000 minimum credit ($150,000 for service corporations).

stem: A C corporation is a personal holding company if five or fewer individuals own more than 50% of its stock and at least what share of its adjusted ordinary gross income is PHC income?

choices.explanation: The income threshold is 60%.
The threshold is 60%.
Correct. Both the ownership test and the 60% income test must be met.
The threshold is 60%.

explanation: IRC §542: a PHC meets the stock ownership test and has PHC income of at least 60% of adjusted ordinary gross income; undistributed PHC income is taxed at 20%.

stem: To join a consolidated return, a subsidiary must be owned by the parent (or other members) at what level?

choices.explanation: 50% is the CFC or control test elsewhere.

choices.text: At least 80% of voting power only
choices.explanation: Value must also meet 80%.
Ownership of 80% is enough.

choices.text: 80% or more of vote and value
choices.explanation: Correct. Affiliated group membership requires 80% of vote and value.

explanation: IRC §1504(a)(2): an includible corporation is owned at least 80% by vote and value by other members.

stem: In a consolidated group, Member S sells land to Member B at a $100,000 gain. B holds the land at year-end. How is the gain treated on the consolidated return?

choices.text: Deferred until B sells outside the group
choices.explanation: Correct. Intercompany gains are deferred until a later event outside the group.
Intercompany transactions are matched to B's later activity.
The gain is deferred, not excluded.

choices.text: Recognized ratably by S over five years
choices.explanation: There is no ratable recognition.

explanation: Reg. §1.1502-13: intercompany items are taken into account under the matching and acceleration rules, generally when the property leaves the group.

stem: A U.S. corporation's pre-credit U.S. tax is $210,000 on worldwide taxable income of $1,000,000, including $200,000 of foreign-source taxable income on which it paid $50,000 of foreign tax. What is its foreign tax credit?

choices.explanation: The credit is limited.
Correct. Limitation = 210,000 × 200,000 ÷ 1,000,000 = 42,000, less than the 50,000 paid.
That is the excess credit, not the credit.
The limitation uses the foreign share of income.

explanation: IRC §904: the foreign tax credit is limited to U.S. tax × foreign-source taxable income ÷ worldwide taxable income; excess credits carry back 1 and forward 10 years.

stem: A partner contributes land (basis $40,000; fair value $100,000) to a partnership. When the partnership later sells the land for $100,000, how is the gain allocated?

choices.text: Among all partners by profit shares
choices.explanation: Built-in gain belongs to the contributor.

choices.text: None, because §721 made the contribution tax-free
choices.explanation: §721 defers, not eliminates, the gain.
Correct. §704(c) allocates the built-in gain to the contributor.

choices.text: Half to the contributor and half to the others
choices.explanation: §704(c) assigns the full built-in gain.

explanation: IRC §704(c): pre-contribution gain or loss is allocated to the contributing partner when the property is sold.

stem: A person receives a 20% capital interest in a partnership, worth $30,000, solely for services. What results?

choices.explanation: §721 covers contributions of property, not services.
Compensation for services is ordinary income.

choices.text: Income only when the partnership is liquidated
choices.explanation: Income arises on receipt of a capital interest.

choices.text: $30,000 ordinary income to the service partner
choices.explanation: Correct. A capital interest received for services is compensation.

explanation: A capital interest received in exchange for services is taxable as ordinary income at its fair value (Reg. §1.721-1(b)).

stem: A partner's outside basis is $8,000 before her $12,000 share of the partnership's ordinary loss. How much loss may she deduct for the year (ignoring at-risk and passive rules)?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses are limited to basis, with the excess suspended.
Losses are limited to basis.
The excess carries forward.
She may deduct up to her basis.

explanation: IRC §704(d): a partner's distributive share of loss is allowed only to the extent of outside basis; the excess carries forward.

stem: In complete liquidation of her interest, a partner with an outside basis of $40,000 receives $30,000 cash only. The partnership has no hot assets. What results?

choices.text: No loss; the remaining basis carries to nothing
choices.explanation: The loss is recognized in this case.
Correct. A loss is recognized when only cash (and hot assets) is received in liquidation.
The loss is capital.
Cash is less than basis.

explanation: IRC §731(a)(2): a partner recognizes loss in a liquidating distribution consisting only of money, unrealized receivables and inventory.

stem: A C corporation converted to S status in 2022 and in 2025 sells land it held at conversion with a $50,000 built-in gain. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: No tax at the entity level for any S corporation
choices.explanation: The BIG tax is an exception.

choices.text: The shareholders pay a 21% penalty tax
choices.explanation: The BIG tax is paid by the corporation.

choices.text: The S corporation owes built-in gains tax at 21%
choices.explanation: Correct. The sale is within the five-year recognition period.

choices.text: Tax applies only after ten years
choices.explanation: The recognition period is five years.

explanation: IRC §1374: an S corporation that was a C corporation pays tax at 21% on net recognized built-in gain within five years after conversion.

stem: A simple trust has $40,000 of taxable interest income and no other items, and must distribute all income to its beneficiary. How much is taxed to the beneficiary?

choices.explanation: The $300 exemption reduces the trust's income, not the beneficiary's share.
All income is required to be distributed.
The beneficiary is taxed on DNI distributed.
Correct. The distribution deduction passes DNI, and its tax, to the beneficiary.

explanation: IRC §651-652: a simple trust deducts income required to be distributed (up to DNI); beneficiaries include that amount.

stem: A client exercises incentive stock options with a $100,000 bargain element and holds the shares. How does the exercise affect her 2025 taxes?

choices.text: $100,000 of ordinary income for regular tax
choices.explanation: ISO exercises don't create regular income.
There is no sale, so no gain.
Correct. The ISO spread is an AMT preference-type adjustment only.

choices.text: No effect on either regular tax or AMT
choices.explanation: The spread affects AMT.

explanation: IRC §56(b)(3): the ISO bargain element is an AMT adjustment in the year of exercise (if the shares are held); AMT paid can create a minimum tax credit.

stem: A client who usually takes the standard deduction gives about $6,000 a year to charity. Which strategy most likely increases the tax benefit of her giving in 2025?

choices.text: Spread the gifts evenly over each month of the year
choices.explanation: Timing within the year doesn't change itemizing.

choices.text: Give cash instead of appreciated stock
choices.explanation: Appreciated stock avoids capital gains tax.

choices.text: Make the gifts to a private foundation
choices.explanation: Foundation gifts have lower AGI limits.

choices.text: Bunch gifts into one year via a donor-advised fund
choices.explanation: Correct. Bunching pushes itemized deductions above the standard deduction in one year.

explanation: Bunching gifts — often through a donor-advised fund — lets the donor itemize in the bunching year and take the standard deduction in others.

stem: For 2025 the kiddie-tax threshold is $2,700. A 15-year-old dependent has $5,000 of interest income and no earned income. How much is taxed at the parents' rate?

choices.explanation: The first $2,700 isn't taxed at the parents' rate.
The threshold is $2,700, not $1,350.
Unearned income above the threshold is taxed at the parents' rate.

explanation: IRC §1(g): a child's net unearned income above the threshold ($2,700 for 2025) is taxed at the parents' rate.

stem: An employee exercises ISOs for 100 shares at $20 when the stock is worth $50 and sells them six months later for $45. What is the result?

choices.explanation: The lesser-of rule limits ordinary income to the gain.
Correct. In a disqualifying disposition, ordinary income is the lesser of the spread (3,000) or the gain (2,500).
The holding periods weren't met.
The gain is compensation income.

explanation: IRC §421(b), §422(c)(2): a disqualifying disposition creates ordinary income equal to the lesser of the exercise spread or the actual gain.

stem: An employee receives restricted stock units that vest in 2025 and settle in shares worth $40,000. When and how is the value taxed?

choices.text: As capital gain when the shares are later sold
choices.explanation: The value at settlement is compensation.

choices.text: At grant, when the units were awarded
choices.explanation: RSUs aren't property at grant.

choices.text: As ordinary income in 2025, at settlement
choices.explanation: Correct. RSUs are taxed as compensation when the shares are delivered.

choices.text: Never, if the employee holds the shares a year
choices.explanation: Holding affects only later appreciation.

explanation: RSUs are unfunded promises; the value of shares delivered at settlement is ordinary income, and it becomes the shares' basis.

stem: A taxpayer qualifies as a real estate professional. Which statement about her rental real estate losses is correct?

choices.text: They are passive and limited to $25,000
choices.explanation: The professional exception removes per se passive treatment.

choices.text: They are deductible without regard to participation
choices.explanation: Material participation is still required.

choices.text: They are capital losses limited to $3,000
choices.explanation: Rental losses are ordinary.
Correct. Real estate professionals who materially participate treat rentals as nonpassive.

explanation: IRC §469(c)(7): a taxpayer with more than 750 hours and more than half of personal services in real property trades treats rentals in which she materially participates as nonpassive.

stem: A taxpayer sells her entire interest in a passive activity to an unrelated buyer in a taxable sale. What happens to $30,000 of suspended passive losses?

choices.text: They are fully deductible in the year of sale
choices.explanation: Correct. A complete taxable disposition frees all suspended losses.

choices.text: They carry over to her other passive activities
choices.explanation: Disposition releases them now.
They are released, not lost.

choices.text: They offset only passive income in later years
choices.explanation: They become fully deductible.

explanation: IRC §469(g): on a fully taxable disposition of the entire interest to an unrelated party, suspended losses are allowed in full.

stem: In 2025 a grandparent contributes $95,000 to a §529 plan for a grandchild and elects to spread it over five years. The annual exclusion is $19,000. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: No Form 709 is ever needed for §529 gifts
choices.explanation: The election requires a return.

choices.text: A Form 709 is required to make the election
choices.explanation: Correct. The five-year election is made on a timely filed gift tax return.

choices.text: The full $95,000 is a 2025 taxable gift
choices.explanation: The election spreads it over five years.

choices.text: The gift uses $76,000 of lifetime exemption
choices.explanation: No exemption is used with the election.

explanation: IRC §529(c)(2)(B): a contributor may elect on Form 709 to treat a gift of up to five times the annual exclusion as made ratably over five years.

stem: A grandparent pays $45,000 of a grandchild's tuition directly to the university in 2025. What taxable gift results?

choices.explanation: The direct-payment tuition exclusion is unlimited.
The tuition exclusion applies.
Correct. Tuition paid directly to an educational institution is excluded without limit.
No taxable gift arises at all.

explanation: IRC §2503(e): tuition paid directly to an educational institution and medical expenses paid directly to the provider are excluded from gifts without limit.

stem: A traditional IRA owner born in 1952 reaches age 73 in 2025. By when must she take her first required minimum distribution?

choices.explanation: She may delay the first RMD until April 1 of the next year.
The deadline is April 1, not the filing date.
No such delay applies.
Correct. The first RMD is due by April 1 of the year after she reaches 73.

explanation: IRC §401(a)(9): the required beginning date is April 1 of the year after the owner reaches the applicable age (73 for those born 1951–1959).

stem: A taxpayer has $6,000 of nondeductible basis in her traditional IRAs, whose total year-end value is $60,000. She converts $6,000 to a Roth IRA. How much of the conversion is taxable?

choices.explanation: Correct. The pro rata rule: 6,000 × (54,000 pretax ÷ 60,000).
The pro rata rule prevents converting only basis.
10% of each dollar converted is nontaxable basis.
That is the nontaxable portion.

explanation: IRC §408(d)(2): all traditional IRAs are aggregated; each distribution is part basis and part pretax in proportion to total basis.

stem: The corporate alternative minimum tax enacted in 2022 applies to:

choices.text: Corporations averaging over $1 billion of book income
choices.explanation: Correct. CAMT is 15% of adjusted financial statement income for applicable corporations.

choices.text: All C corporations with any taxable income
choices.explanation: CAMT applies only to very large corporations.

choices.text: Corporations with gross receipts over $7.5 million a year
choices.explanation: That was the small corporation test for the old AMT.
S corporations aren't subject to CAMT.

explanation: IRC §55(b)(2), §59(k): applicable corporations (average annual AFSI above $1 billion) pay a 15% minimum tax on AFSI.

stem: Which is a principal advantage of filing a consolidated return?

choices.text: Each member uses its own tax year
choices.explanation: All members must adopt the parent's year.
Correct. Consolidation combines members' income and losses.

choices.text: Members may elect different accounting periods
choices.explanation: All use the parent's period.
They are deferred.

explanation: A consolidated return combines members' taxable income, so losses of one offset income of another, and intercompany transactions are deferred.

stem: A foreign corporation is a controlled foreign corporation when U.S. shareholders — each owning at least 10% — together own:

choices.text: At least 25% of its vote and value
choices.explanation: The test is more than 50%.
The test is more than 50%.

choices.text: More than 50% of its vote or value
choices.explanation: Correct. That is the CFC test.

choices.text: Any shares listed on a U.S. exchange
choices.explanation: Listing isn't the test.

explanation: IRC §957(a), §951(b): a CFC is more than 50% owned (vote or value) by U.S. shareholders, each owning at least 10%.

stem: For a special allocation in a partnership agreement to be respected, it must have:

choices.text: The approval of the IRS in advance
choices.explanation: No IRS approval is required.
Special allocations are by nature unequal.
Business purpose alone isn't the standard.
Correct. §704(b) respects allocations with substantial economic effect.

explanation: IRC §704(b): allocations are respected if they have substantial economic effect or match the partners' interests in the partnership.

stem: Purchasing a partnership interest when the partnership's assets have appreciated, the buyer wants a basis step-up in her share of those assets. The partnership should have in effect:

choices.explanation: Correct. It enables a §743(b) adjustment for the purchaser.
That is a corporate election.
That concerns expensing.
That concerns property received for services.

explanation: With a §754 election (or a substantial built-in loss), the partnership adjusts the purchaser's share of inside basis under §743(b).

stem: A partner sells her interest at a $50,000 gain; her share of the partnership's unrealized receivables would produce $15,000 of ordinary income. How is the gain characterized?

choices.explanation: §751 carves out ordinary income.
Correct. §751 makes the portion tied to hot assets ordinary.
Only the hot-asset portion is ordinary.
That reverses the split.

explanation: IRC §751(a): gain on the sale of a partnership interest is ordinary to the extent attributable to unrealized receivables and inventory.

stem: An S corporation with accumulated E&P of $5,000 from C years has AAA of $10,000. It distributes $13,000 to its sole shareholder (stock basis $40,000). How is the distribution taxed?

choices.explanation: Accumulated E&P is reached after AAA.
AAA is distributed tax-free first.
Correct. Distributions come first from AAA, then from accumulated E&P.

choices.text: $5,000 dividend and $8,000 tax-free return of basis
choices.explanation: AAA comes before E&P.

explanation: IRC §1368(c): with accumulated E&P, distributions come from AAA (tax-free to basis), then E&P (dividends), then remaining basis.

stem: A complex trust's trustee distributes income on February 20, 2026. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: It must be treated as a 2026 distribution
choices.explanation: The 65-day election is available.

choices.text: It is taxed to the trust in both years
choices.explanation: No double taxation arises.
Distributions don't affect the exemption.
Correct. The 65-day rule allows that election.

explanation: IRC §663(b): distributions within the first 65 days of the tax year may be elected as made on the last day of the prior year.

stem: A §501(c)(3) charity has $50,000 of gross unrelated business income and $20,000 of directly connected expenses. What is its unrelated business taxable income?

choices.explanation: Correct. 50,000 − 20,000 − 1,000 specific deduction.
The $1,000 specific deduction applies.
Directly connected expenses are deductible.
UBTI from unrelated business is taxable.

explanation: IRC §512: UBTI is gross income from an unrelated trade or business less directly connected deductions and a $1,000 specific deduction; Form 990-T is required.
